titulo: Inside Google (1/3): where the money comes from 💵 #shorts
descripcion:
Inside the Magnificent 7 · Google, part 1 of 3: where the money comes from. Data from the Q3 2026 earnings release (Jul–Sep) and Google's official blog.

💵 Revenue: $127.6B (+25%) · Search $63.4B (+12%) · Cloud $30.7B (+103%, operating income $11.1B) · Subscriptions, Play & devices $14.3B · YouTube ads $11.2B · Ad network $7.5B
📺 150M YouTube Music & Premium subscribers (incl. trials)
📊 Operating margin 31.8% · Ads: 72.5% → 64.3% of revenue in one year

escenas.texto: Google sold one hundred twenty seven point six billion dollars in three months. That's a pace of half a trillion a year. Where does all that money come from? This is part one of three.
Sixty three billion came from search. Thirty one from the cloud. Fourteen from subscriptions, the Play Store and phones. Eleven from YouTube ads. And seven and a half from ads on other sites.

visual.pre: where the money comes from (3 months)

escenas.texto: Search is still king, growing twelve percent. The fear was that chatbots would kill it, but Google's own CEO said it: searches are growing at the fastest pace in five years.
But the star is the cloud. In one year, quarterly sales went from fifteen billion to thirty point seven billion. And its profit tripled: from three point six to eleven point one billion.
That's why Google depends less and less on ads: advertising went from seventy two to sixty four percent of everything it sells.
And YouTube isn't just ads anymore: between Music and Premium it has one hundred fifty million subscribers.
In the end, out of every hundred dollars it sells, almost thirty two are operating profit.
In part two: what Google is researching. Its own chips, a Nobel Prize, driverless taxis and a quantum computer. Subscribe so you don't miss it.
